Returns (payload_json, type_field_value):\n///    - For 'skip' types: (empty object, None) to drop the line\n///    - For 'meta' types: (empty object, Some(type_value))\n///    - For 'event' types: type field value\n    // Read the type_field from the JSON value using envelope.type_field\n    let type_value = raw_json\n        .get(&envelope.type_field)\n        .and_then(|v| match v {\n            Value::String(s) => Some(s.clone()),\n            Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n            Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n            _ => None,\n        })\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    let routing = envelope.get_routing(&type_value);\n\n    match routing {\n        \"skip\" => {\n            // Return empty payload with None to signal \"drop this line\"\n            Ok((Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()), None))\n        }\n        \"meta\" => {\n            // Return empty payload with the full wrapper JSON\n            Ok((\n                Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),\n                Some(raw_json.clone()),\n            ))\n        }\n        \"event\" => {\n            // Extract payload from payload_field\n            let extracted = raw_json.get(&envelope.payload_field).and_then(|v| {\n                // Only use if it's an object (not a string/null/etc)\n                match v {\n                    Value::Object(_) => Some(v),\n                    _ => None,\n                }\n            });\n\n            match extracted {\n                Some(payload) => {\n                    // Return the extracted payload along with the full wrapper JSON\n                    Ok((payload.clone(), Some(raw_json.clone())))\n                }\n                None => {\n                    // Missing or non-object payload_field - skip with warning\n                    // Determine specific warning reason\n                    let has_payload_field = raw_json.get(&envelope.payload_field).is_some();\n                    let warning_msg = if has_payload_field {\n                        let payload_value = raw_json.get(&envelope.payload_field).unwrap();\n                        let value_desc = match payload_value {\n                            Value::String(s) => {\n                                let truncated = if s.len() > 50 {\n                                    format!(\"{}...\", &s[..50])\n                                } else {\n                                    s.clone()\n                                };\n                                format!(\"string '{}'\", truncated)\n                            }\n                            Value::Null => \"null\".to_string(),\n                            Value::Bool(b) => format!(\"bool {}\", b),\n                            Value::Number(n) => format!(\"number {}\", n),\n                            Value::Array(_) => \"array\".to_string(),\n                            Value::Object(_) => \"object\".to_string(),\n                        };\n                        format!(\n                            \"Envelope payload_field '{}' exists for type '{}' but is not an object (found: {}), skipping line\",\n                            envelope.payload_field, type_value, value_desc\n                        )\n                    } else {\n                        format!(\n                            \"Envelope payload_field '{}' missing for type '{}', skipping line\",\n                            envelope.payload_field, type_value\n                        )\n                    };\n                    warn!(\"{}\", warning_msg);\n                    Ok((Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()), None))\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        _ => {\n            // Unknown routing (shouldn't happen due to get_routing defaults, but handle defensively)\n            Ok((Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()), None))\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Opens a file, optionally decompressing if it has a .zst extension\nfn open_file_maybe_zst(path: &Path) -> Result<Box<dyn BufRead>> {\n    let file = std::fs::File::open(path)?;\n\n    if path.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) == Some(\"zst\") {\n        // Use streaming zstd decompression\n        let decoder =\n            zstd::stream::read::Decoder::new(file).map_err(|e| AgentScribeError::Parse {\n                file: path.display().to_string(),\n                line: Some(0),\n                message: format!(\"Zstd decompression error: {}\", e),\n            })?;\n        Ok(Box::new(BufReader::new(decoder)))\n    } else {\n        Ok(Box::new(BufReader::new(file)))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl JsonlParser {\n    /// Parse a single JSONL line into an event\n    pub fn parse_line(\n        line: &str,\n        line_number: usize,\n        context: &ParseContext,\n        plugin: &Plugin,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        let raw_json: Value = serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| {\n            AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                format!(\"Invalid JSON: {}\", e),\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // --- Envelope routing and payload unwrapping ---\n        // When the plugin defines [source.envelope], the JSONL line is a wrapper:\n        //   { type_field: \"...\", payload_field: { ... actual event ... } }\n        // Type routing determines whether to produce events, skip, or capture metadata.\n        //\n        // Set up envelope_json and payload_json references:\n        // - envelope_json: reference to the full parsed line (or None if no envelope)\n        // - payload_json: reference to the event data (from payload_field if envelope, else full line)\n        //\n        // Field extraction uses envelope-aware functions:\n        // - Fields starting with '^' read from envelope_json\n        // - Fields without '^' read from payload_json\n\n        let (envelope_json, payload_json): (Option<&Value>, &Value) = if let Some(\n            ref envelope_cfg,\n        ) = plugin.source.envelope\n        {\n            // Envelope mode: extract type and apply routing\n            let type_value =\n                extract_string(&raw_json, &envelope_cfg.type_field).unwrap_or_default();\n            let routing = envelope_cfg.get_routing(&type_value);\n\n            match routing {\n                \"skip\" => {\n                    // Skip this line - no event emitted\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n                \"meta\" => {\n                    // Metadata line - no event emitted\n                    // TODO: Future session metadata accumulation (project, model, version)\n                    // These lines contain session-level metadata that should be extracted\n                    // and accumulated into the session context. For now, we drop them.\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n                \"event\" => {\n                    // Extract payload from payload_field for event body\n                    let extracted = raw_json.get(&envelope_cfg.payload_field).and_then(|v| {\n                        // Only use if it's an object (not a string/null/etc)\n                        match v {\n                            Value::Object(_) => Some(v),\n                            _ => None,\n                        }\n                    });\n\n                    match extracted {\n                        Some(payload) => {\n                            // Valid payload object extracted\n                            (Some(&raw_json), payload)\n                        }\n                        None => {\n                            // Missing or non-object payload_field - skip with warning\n                            // Determine specific warning reason\n                            let has_payload_field =\n                                raw_json.get(&envelope_cfg.payload_field).is_some();\n                            let warning_msg = if has_payload_field {\n                                let payload_value =\n                                    raw_json.get(&envelope_cfg.payload_field).unwrap();\n                                let value_desc = match payload_value {\n                                    Value::String(s) => {\n                                        let truncated = if s.len() > 50 {\n                                            format!(\"{}...\", &s[..50])\n                                        } else {\n                                            s.clone()\n                                        };\n                                        format!(\"string '{}'\", truncated)\n                                    }\n                                    Value::Null => \"null\".to_string(),\n                                    Value::Bool(b) => format!(\"bool {}\", b),\n                                    Value::Number(n) => format!(\"number {}\", n),\n                                    Value::Array(_) => \"array\".to_string(),\n                                    Value::Object(_) => \"object\".to_string(),\n                                };\n                                format!(\n                                    \"Envelope payload_field '{}' exists for type '{}' but is not an object (found: {}), skipping line\",\n                                    envelope_cfg.payload_field, type_value, value_desc\n                                )\n                            } else {\n                                format!(\n                                    \"Envelope payload_field '{}' missing for type '{}', skipping line\",\n                                    envelope_cfg.payload_field, type_value\n                                )\n                            };\n                            warn!(\"{}\", warning_msg);\n                            return Ok(Vec::new());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {\n                    // Unknown routing (shouldn't happen due to get_routing defaults, but handle defensively)\n                    return Ok(Vec::new());\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // No envelope: both envelope_json and payload_json point to the full line\n            (None, &raw_json)\n        };\n\n        // Check type filter (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        if let Some(ref filter) = plugin.parser.include_types {\n            let type_field = &filter.field;\n            if let Some(type_val) =\n                extract_string_with_envelope(type_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n            {\n                if !filter.values.contains(&type_val) {\n                    return Ok(Vec::new()); // Skip this event\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref filter) = plugin.parser.exclude_types {\n            let type_field = &filter.field;\n            if let Some(type_val) =\n                extract_string_with_envelope(type_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n            {\n                if filter.values.contains(&type_val) {\n                    return Ok(Vec::new()); // Skip this event\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Parse timestamp (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let ts = if let Some(ref ts_field) = plugin.parser.timestamp {\n            parse_timestamp_with_envelope(ts_field, payload_json, envelope_json).map_err(|e| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Timestamp error: {}\", e),\n                )\n            })?\n        } else {\n            Utc::now() // Fallback - shouldn't happen with validation\n        };\n\n        // Parse role (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let role_str = if let Some(ref role_field) = plugin.parser.role {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(role_field, payload_json, envelope_json).ok_or_else(\n                || {\n                    AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                        &context.source_file,\n                        line_number,\n                        format!(\"Role field '{}' not found\", role_field),\n                    )\n                },\n            )?\n        } else {\n            return Err(AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                \"No role field configured\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        };\n\n        // Apply role mapping\n        let role = if let Some(mapped) = plugin.parser.role_map.get(&role_str) {\n            Role::from_str(mapped).ok_or_else(|| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Invalid role mapping: {}\", mapped),\n                )\n            })?\n        } else {\n            Role::from_str(&role_str).ok_or_else(|| {\n                AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                    &context.source_file,\n                    line_number,\n                    format!(\"Invalid role: {}\", role_str),\n                )\n            })?\n        };\n\n        // Parse content (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let content = if let Some(ref content_field) = plugin.parser.content {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(content_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .unwrap_or_default()\n        } else {\n            return Err(AgentScribeError::parse_error_with_line(\n                &context.source_file,\n                line_number,\n                \"No content field configured\".to_string(),\n            ));\n        };\n\n        // Build base event\n        let mut event = Event::new(\n            ts,\n            context.session_id.clone(),\n            context.source_agent.clone(),\n            role,\n            content,\n        );\n\n        // Extract tool name (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        // Note: This extraction is not restricted to tool_call/tool_result roles to allow\n        // the tool_name field to be used for general envelope field extraction (e.g., testing\n        // that ^model correctly reads from the envelope layer via tool_name: Some(\"^model\"))\n        if let Some(ref tool_field) = plugin.parser.tool_name {\n            if let Some(tool_name) =\n                extract_string_with_envelope(tool_field, payload_json, envelope_json)\n            {\n                event.tool = Some(tool_name);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Extract tokens (envelope-aware: ^ prefix reads from wrapper, otherwise from payload)\n        let tokens_in = plugin.parser.tokens_in.as_ref().and_then(|f| {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(f, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n        });\n        let tokens_out = plugin.parser.tokens_out.as_ref().and_then(|f| {\n            extract_string_with_envelope(f, payload_json, envelope_json)\n                .and_then(|s| s.parse::<u32>().ok())\n        });\n\n        if tokens_in.is_some() || tokens_out.is_some() {\n            event.tokens = Some(TokenCounts {\n                input: tokens_in.unwrap_or(0),\n                output: tokens_out.unwrap_or(0),\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Set project from context\n        event.project = context.project.clone();\n\n        // Set model from context\n        event.model = context.model.clone();\n\n        // Add static fields\n        for (key, value) in &plugin.parser.static_fields {\n            match key.as_str() {\n                \"source_agent\" => {\n                    if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                        // Only override if we don't already have a subagent suffix\n                        // The ParseContext sets source_agent with \"-subagent\" suffix for subagent files,\n                        // and we need to                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                \"source_version\" => {\n                    if let Some(s) = value.as_str() {\n                        event.source_version = Some(s.to_string());\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => {}\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Handle event expansion for compound events (e.g., Claude Code tool_use blocks)\n        // For now, return single event - expansion can be added per-agent\n        Ok(vec![event])\n    }\n}\n\nimpl super::FormatParser for JsonlParser {\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        let reader = open_file_maybe_zst(source_path)?;\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // Get session ID from filename\n        let session_id = match &plugin.source.session_detection {\n            SessionDetection::OneFilePerSession { session_id_from } => {\n                match session_id_from {\n                    SessionIdSource::Filename => {\n                        // For subagent sessions, include parent directory in session ID\n                        // to maintain hierarchy and avoid collisions\n                        let is_subagent = is_subagent_file(source_path);\n\n                        eprintln!(\"DEBUG: source_path = {:?}\", source_path);\n                        eprintln!(\"DEBUG: is_subagent = {}\", is_subagent);\n\n                        if is_subagent {\n                            // Extract path from .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                                                .to_string()\n                                        }\n                                    } else {\n .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                                            .to_string()\n                                    }\n                                } else {\n          } else {\n                        return Err(e);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: SessionDetection::OneFilePerSession { session_id_from } => {\n                let session_id = match session_id_from {\n                    SessionIdSource::Filename => {\n                        // .and_then(|s| s.to_str())\n                                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                                        .to_string()\n                                }\n                       {\n                                            let type_value =\n                                                extract_string(&json, &envelope_cfg.type_field)\n \"unknown\".to_string()\n                                }\n                            }\n                            Err(_) => \"unknown\".to_string(),\n                        }\n     // The parent session is the component immediately before \"subagents\"\n                            let parent_idx = subagents_idx - 1;\n\n                            components\n                                .get(parent_idx)\n                                .and_then(|c| c.as_os_str().to_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                        } else {\n                            None\n                        }\n                    });\n\n                Ok(vec![SessionInfo {\n                    session_id,\n                    start_offset: 0,\n                    end_offset: file_size,\n                    metadata: None,\n                    parent_session_id,\n                }])\n            }\n            _ => {\n                // For other detection methods, we'd need to parse the whole file\n                // For Phase 1, we only support one-file-per-session for JSONL\n                Ok(vec![])\n            }\n        }\n Import equality and comparison\n223\t///\n224\t/// ```rust\n225\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n226\t///\n227\t/// let import1 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n228\t/// let import2 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n229\t/// let import3 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n230\t///\n231\t/// // Same path, type, and line number are equal\n232\t/// assert_eq!(import1, import2);\n233\t///\n234\t/// // Different line numbers are not equal\n235\t/// assert_ne!(import1, import3);\n236\t/// ```\n237\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]\n238\tpub struct Import {\n239\t    /// The import path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`, `\"crate::module::Item\"`)\n240\t    ///\n241\t    /// Contains the full module path being imported. The format varies by import type:\n242\t    ///\n243\t    /// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n244\t    ///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n245\t    /// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n246\t    /// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n247\t    ///\n248\t    /// # Valid Values\n249\t    ///\n250\t    /// - Non-empty string (cannot be `\"\"`)\n251\t    /// - Contains only valid Rust identifier characters and path separators (`::`)\n252\t    /// - Case-sensitive (matches Rust's naming rules)\n253\t    /// - May include standard library prefixes (`std::`, `core::`, `alloc::`)\n254\t    /// - May include crate-relative paths (`crate::`, `super::`, `self`)\n255\t    ///\n256\t    /// # Examples\n257\t    ///\n258\t    /// ```rust\n259\t    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n260\t    ///\n261\t    /// // Standard library import\n262\t    /// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n263\t    /// assert_eq!(std_import.path, \"std::collections::HashMap\");\n264\t    ///\n265\t    /// // External crate import\n266\t    /// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n267\t    /// assert_eq!(extern_import.path, \"serde\");\n268\t    ///\n269\t    /// // Crate-relative import\n270\t    /// let crate_import = Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n271\t    /// assert_eq!(crate_import.path, \"crate::module::Item\");\n272\t    /// ```\n273\t    pub path: String,\n274\t\n275\t    /// Type of import statement ([`ImportType::Use`], [`ImportType::ExternCrate`], or [`ImportType::Mod`])\n276\t    ///\n277\t    /// Distinguishes between the three fundamental kinds of import statements in Rust.\n278\t    /// This classification is essential for categorizing imports and understanding their\n279\t    /// role in the module structure.\n280\t    ///\n281\t    /// # Valid Values\n282\t    ///\n283\t    /// Only the three variants defined in [`ImportType`]:\n284\t    ///\n285\t    /// - **[`ImportType::Use`]**: Standard `use` statements for importing items from modules,\n286\t    ///   crates, or other scopes. Most common import type.\n287\t    ///\n288\t    /// - **[`ImportType::ExternCrate`]**: External crate declarations. Required in Rust 2015\n289\t    ///   edition, largely obsolete in Rust 2018+ but still used in specific contexts.\n290\t    ///\n291\t    /// - **[`ImportType::Mod`]**: Module declarations that define the module structure,\n292\t    ///   either file-based (`mod foo;`) or inline (`mod bar { ... }`).\n293\t    ///\n294\t    /// # Usage in Practice\n295\t    ///\n296\t    /// ```rust\n297\t External crates are not std lib\n304\t    ///         ImportType::Mod => false,  // Module declarations are not std lib imports\n305\t    ///     }\n306\t    /// }\n307\t    ///\n308\t    /// let Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n312\t    /// assert!(!is_standard_library(&extern_import));\n313\t    /// ```\n314\t    ///\n315\t    /// # Examples\n316\t    ///\n317\t    /// ```rust\n318\t    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n319\t    ///\n320\t    /// let use_import = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n321\t assert_eq!(mod_import.import_type, ImportType::Mod);\n328\t    /// ```\n329\t    pub import_type: ImportType,\n330\t\n331\t    /// Line number where the import appears (1-indexed)\n332\t    ///\n333\t    /// Represents the position in the source file where this import statement is located.\n334\t    /// Line numbers start at 1 (not 0) to match standard text editor and compiler line numbering.\n335\t    ///\n336\t    /// # Valid Values\n337\t    ///\n338\t    /// - Must be ≥ 1 (1-indexed, not 0-indexed)\n339\t    /// - Should be ≤ total lines in the source file\n340\t    /// -   /// - **Error reporting**: Point users to the exact location of problematic imports\n347\t    /// - **Import organization**: Sort or group imports by their position in the file\n348\t    /// - **Tool integration**: IDE features, linters, and code analysis tools\n349\t    /// - **Diffs and patches**: Track import location changes between file versions\n350\t    ///\n351\t    /// # Examples\n352\t    ///\n353\t    /// ```rust\n354\t    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n355\t    ///\n356\t    /// // Track import location for error reporting\n357\t    /// let JSON using dot notation\n455\tpub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n456\t    if path.is_empty() {\n457\t        return None;\n458\t    }\n459\t\n460\t    let mut current = value;\n461\t    for part in path.split('.') {\n462\t        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n463\t        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n464\t            let key = &part[..bracket_pos];\n465\t            let index_str = &part[bracket_pos + 1..part.len() - 1];\n466\t            let index: usize = index_str.parse().ok()?;\n467\t\n468\t            current = current.get(key)?.get(index)?;\n469\t        } else {\n470\t            current = current.get(part)?;\n471\t        }\n472\t    }\n473\t    Some(current.clone())\n474\t}\n475\t\n476\t/// Extract a string field from JSON\n477\tpub fn extract_string(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n478\t    let field = extract_field(value, path)?;\n479\t    match field {\n480\t        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n481\t        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n482\t        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n483\t        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n484\t        _ => None,\n485\t    }\n486\t}\n487\t\n488\t/// Parse timestamp from various formats\n489\tpub fn parse_timestamp(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n490\t    let ts_str = extract_string(value, path)\n491\t        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n492\t\n493\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n494\t    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n495\t        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n496\t    }\n497\t\n498\t    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n499\t    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n500\t        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n501\t            // Milliseconds\n502\t            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n503\t        } else {\n504\t            // Seconds\n505\t            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n506\t        };\n507\t        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n508\t    }\n509\t\n510\t    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n511\t    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n512\t        return Ok(dt);\n513\t    }\n514\t\n515\t    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n516\t        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n517\t        ts_str\n518\t    )))\n519\t}\n520\t\n521\t/// Extract a field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n522\t///\n523\t/// **Envelope-first with payload fallback for caret-prefixed paths:**\n524\t/// - If path starts with `^`, try envelope first (remove `^` prefix)\n525\t/// - If envelope is None OR field not found in envelope, fallback to payload\n526\t/// - Otherwise, extract from payload only\n527\t///\n528\t/// **Resolution order for (e.g., `^outer.ts` or `user.role`)\n537\t/// and array indexing (e.g., `items[0].name`).\n538\tpub fn extract_with_envelope(\n539\t    path: &str,\n540\t    payload: &Value,\n541\t    envelope: payload only\n560\t        extract_field(payload, path)\n561\t    }\n562\t}\n563\t\n564\t/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n565\t///\n566\t/// Wrapper extract_string_with_envelope(\n569\t    path: &str,\n570\t    payload: &Value,\n571\t    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n572\t) -> Option<String> {\n573\t    let value = extract_with_envelope(path,          })\n596\t                .collect();\n597\t            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n598\t                None\n599\t            } else {\n600\t                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n601\t            }\n602\t        }\n603\t        _ => None,\n604\t    }\n605\t}\n606\t\n607\t/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n608\t///\n609\t/// This module provides types for working with Rust import statements:\n//!\n//! - **[`Import`]**: Lightweight struct representing a single import statement with path,\n//!   type, and line number information\n//! - **[`ImportType`]**: Enum representing the three kinds of Rust import statements\n//!   (`use`, `extern crate`, and `mod`)\n//!\n//! ## When to Use These Types\n//!\n//! Use these types when you need to:\n//! - Parse and analyze Rust source files for their import dependencies\n//! - Categorize imports by type (standard `use` statements vs extern crates vs modules)\n//! - Track the location of imports within source files\n//! - Build tools that work with Rust module structures\n//!\n//! ## Example\n//!\n//! ```\n//! use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n//!\n//! // Create an import representing: use std::collections::HashMap;\n//! let import = Import::new(\n//!     \"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(),\n//! For full parsing functionality including multi-file import extraction,\n//! see the `ImportParser` type which provides parsing of complete Rust source files.\n\nmod aider_input;\nmod import_parser;\nmod json_array;\nmod json_tree;\nmod jsonl;\nmod markdown;\nmod sqlite;\n\npub use aider_input::{AiderInputEntry, AiderInputHistory};\npub use import_parser::{ImportParseResult, ImportParser, ImportStatement, ImportType};\npub use json_array::JsonArrayParser;\npub use json_tree::JsonTreeParser;\npub use jsonl::JsonlParser;\npub use markdown::MarkdownParser;\npub use sqlite::SqliteParser;\n\n/// Lightweight representation of a Rust import statement\n///\n/// A simplified struct containing the essential information about a single import statement\n/// found in Rust source code. This struct focuses on the core attributes needed for import\n/// analysis and categorization.\n///\n/// # When to Use Import vs ImportStatement\n///\n/// The [`Import`] struct is a lightweight alternative to [`ImportStatement`]:\n///\n/// - **Use [`Import`]** when you need basic import information without the overhead of\n///   storing the original source line. Ideal for:\n///   - Import categorization and counting\n///   - Dependency analysis\n///   - Module structure mapping\n///   - Lightweight tooling\n///\n/// - **Use [`ImportStatement`]** when you need the complete original text including:\n///   - Exact formatting and whitespace\n///   - Comments in import statements\n///   - Multi-line import blocks\n///   - Source reconstruction\n///\n/// # Field Documentation\n///\n/// ## `path: String`\n///\n/// The import path extracted from the import statement. The format varies by import type:\n///\n/// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path being imported (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n/// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n/// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n///\n/// **Constraints:**\n/// - Non-empty string (cannot be `\"\"`)\n/// - Contains only valid Rust identifier characters and path separators (`::`)\n/// - Case-sensitive (matches Rust's rules)\n///\n/// **Usage in practice:**\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// // Standard library import\n/// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n///\n/// // Crate-relative import\n/// let crate_import = Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n///\n/// // External crate\n/// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## `import_type: ImportType`\n///\n/// The type classification of the import statement. This field distinguishes between the three\n/// fundamental kinds of import statements in Rust:\n///\n/// - **[`ImportType::Use`]**: Standard `use` statements (most common)\n/// - **[`ImportType::ExternCrate`]**: External crate declarations\n/// - **[`ImportType::Mod`]**: Module declarations\n///\n/// **Valid values:** Only the three variants defined in [`ImportType`]\n///\n/// **Usage in practice:**\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// // Categorize imports by type\n/// fn is_standard_library(import: &Import) -> bool {\n///     match import.import_type {\n///         ImportType::Use => import.path.starts_with(\"std::\") || import.path.starts_with(\"core::\"),\n///         _ => false,\n///     }\n/// }\n///\n/// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n/// assert!(is_standard_library(&std_import));\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## `line_number: usize`\n///\n/// The 1-indexed line number where the import statement appears in the source file.\n///\n/// **Constraints:**\n/// - Must be ≥ 1 (1-indexed, not 0-indexed)\n/// - Should be ≤ total lines in the source file\n/// - Used for source location and error reporting\n///\n/// **Usage in practice:**\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// // Track import location for error reporting\n/// let import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 42);\n///\n/// println!(\"Import found at line {}\", import.line_number);\n/// // Output: Import found at line 42\n///\n/// // Compare import locations\n/// let import1 = Import::new(\"foo\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n/// let import2 = Import::new(\"bar\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 20);\n///\n/// assert!(import1.line_number < import2.line_number);\n/// ```\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Creating different import types\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// // Create a standard library use import\n/// let std_import = Import::new(\n///     \"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(),\n///     ImportType::Use,\n///     15\n/// );\n///\n/// // Create an external crate import\n/// let extern_import = Import::new(\n///     \"serde\".to_string(),\n///     ImportType::ExternCrate,\n///     3\n/// );\n///\n/// // Create a module declaration\n/// let mod_import = Import::new(\n///     \"my_module\".to_string(),\n///     ImportType::Mod,\n///     8\n/// );\n///\n/// assert_eq!(std_import.import_type, ImportType::Use);\n/// assert_eq!(extern_import.import_type, ImportType::ExternCrate);\n/// assert_eq!(mod_import.import_type, ImportType::Mod);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Working with imports programmatically\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// let imports = vec![\n///     Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5),\n///     Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1),\n///     Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10),\n/// ];\n///\n/// // Count imports by type\n/// let use_count = imports.iter()\n///     .filter(|i| i.import_type == ImportType::Use)\n///     .count();\n///\n/// assert_eq!(use_count, 2);\n///\n/// // Find standard library imports\n/// let std_libs: Vec<_> = imports.iter()\n///     .filter(|i| i.path.starts_with(\"std::\"))\n///     .collect();\n///\n/// assert_eq!(std_libs.len(), 1);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Import equality and comparison\n///\n/// ```rust\n/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n///\n/// let import1 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n/// let import2 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n/// let import3 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n///\n/// // Same path, type, and line number are equal\n/// assert_eq!(import1, import2);\n///\n/// // Different line numbers are not equal\n/// assert_ne!(import1, import3);\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]\npub struct Import {\n    /// The import path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`, `\"crate::module::Item\"`)\n    ///\n    /// Contains the full module path being imported. The format varies by import type:\n    ///\n    /// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n    ///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n    /// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n    /// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n    ///\n    /// # Valid Values\n    ///\n    /// - Non-empty string (cannot be `\"\"`)\n    /// - Contains only valid Rust identifier characters and path separators (`::`)\n    /// - Case-sensitive (matches Rust's naming rules)\n    /// - May include standard library prefixes (`std::`, `core::`, `alloc::`)\n    /// - May include crate-relative paths (`crate::`, `super::`, `self`)\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust\n    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n    ///\n    /// // Standard library import\n    /// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n    /// assert_eq!(std_import.path, \"std::collections::HashMap\");\n    ///\n    /// // External crate import\n    /// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n    /// assert_eq!(extern_import.path, \"serde\");\n    ///\n    /// // Crate-relative import\n    /// let crate_import = Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n    /// assert_eq!(crate_import.path, \"crate::module::Item\");\n    /// ```\n    pub path: String,\n\n    /// Type of import statement ([`ImportType::Use`], [`ImportType::ExternCrate`], or [`ImportType::Mod`])\n    ///\n    /// Distinguishes between the three fundamental kinds of import statements in Rust.\n    /// This classification is essential for categorizing imports and understanding their\n    /// role in the module structure.\n    ///\n    /// # Valid Values\n    ///\n    /// Only the three variants defined in [`ImportType`]:\n    ///\n    /// - **[`ImportType::Use`]**: Standard `use` statements for importing items from modules,\n    ///   crates, or other scopes. Most common import type.\n    ///\n    /// - **[`ImportType::ExternCrate`]**: External crate declarations. Required in Rust 2015\n    ///   edition, largely obsolete in Rust 2018+ but still used in specific contexts.\n    ///\n    /// - **[`ImportType::Mod`]**: Module declarations that define the module structure,\n    ///   either file-based (`mod foo;`) or inline (`mod bar { ... }`).\n    ///\n    /// # Usage in Practice\n    ///\n    /// ```rust\n    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n    ///\n    /// // Filter imports by type\n    /// fn is_standard_library(import: &Import) -> bool {\n    ///     match import.import_type {\n    ///         ImportType::Use => import.path.starts_with(\"std::\") || import.path.starts_with(\"core::\"),\n    ///         ImportType::ExternCrate => false,  // External crates are not std lib\n    ///         ImportType::Mod => false,  // Module declarations are not std lib imports\n    ///     }\n    /// }\n    ///\n    /// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n    /// assert!(is_standard_library(&std_import));\n    ///\n    /// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n    /// assert!(!is_standard_library(&extern_import));\n    /// ```\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust\n    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n    ///\n    /// let use_import = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n    /// assert_eq!(use_import.import_type, ImportType::Use);\n    ///\n    /// let extern_import = Import::new(\"tokio\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n    /// assert_eq!(extern_import.import_type, ImportType::ExternCrate);\n    ///\n    /// let mod_import = Import::new(\"my_module\".to_string(), ImportType::Mod, 10);\n    /// assert_eq!(mod_import.import_type, ImportType::Mod);\n    /// ```\n    pub import_type: ImportType,\n\n    /// Line number where the import appears (1-indexed)\n    ///\n    /// Represents the position in the source file where this import statement is located.\n    /// Line numbers start at 1 (not 0) to match standard text editor and compiler line numbering.\n    ///\n    /// # Valid Values\n    ///\n    /// - Must be ≥ 1 (1-indexed, not 0-indexed)\n    /// - Should be ≤ total lines in the source file\n    /// - Used for source location, error reporting, and tool positioning\n    ///\n    /// # Usage in Practice\n    ///\n    /// This field is particularly useful for:\n    ///\n    /// - **Error reporting**: Point users to the exact location of problematic imports\n    /// - **Import organization**: Sort or group imports by their position in the file\n    /// - **Tool integration**: IDE features, linters, and code analysis tools\n    /// - **Diffs and patches**: Track import location changes between file versions\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```rust\n    /// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n    ///\n    /// // Track import location for error reporting\n    /// let import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 42);\n    ///\n    /// println!(\"Import found at line {}\", import.line_number);\n    /// // Output: Import found at line 42\n    ///\n    /// // Sort imports by line number\n    /// let mut imports = vec![\n    ///     Import::new(\"crate::b\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 20),\n    ///     Import::new(\"crate::a\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10),\n    ///     Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5),\n    /// ];\n    ///\n    /// imports.sort_by(|a, b| a.line_number.cmp(&b.line_number));\n    ///\n    /// assert_eq!(imports[0].line_number, 5);\n    /// assert_eq!(imports[1].line_number, 10);\n    /// assert_eq!(imports[2].line_number, 20);\n    /// ```\n    pub line_number: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Import {\n    /// Create a new import\n    pub fn new(path: String, import_type: ImportType, line_number: usize) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            path,\n            import_type,\n            line_number,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nuse crate::error::{AgentScribeError, Result};\nuse crate::event::Event;\nuse crate::plugin::Plugin;\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse serde_json::Value;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n/// Context for parsing - contains info about the source file and session\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub struct ParseContext {\n    pub session_id: String,\n    pub source_agent: String,\n    pub source_file: String,\n    pub project: Option<String>,\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    pub line_number: usize,\n}\n\nimpl ParseContext {\n    pub fn new(session_id: String, source_agent: String, source_file: String) -> Self {\n        ParseContext {\n            session_id,\n            source_agent,\n            source_file,\n            project: None,\n            model: None,\n            line_number: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn with_project(mut self, project: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        self.project = project;\n        self\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn with_model(mut self, model: Option<String>) -> Self {\n        self.model = model;\n        self\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn increment_line(&mut self) {\n        self.line_number += 1;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a field name has a caret prefix (^)\n///\n/// Returns true if the field name starts with `^`, false otherwise.\n/// Handles empty strings gracefully (returns false).\n///\n/// # Examples\n/// ```\n/// assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"foo\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"bar^baz\"));\n/// assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\"\"));\n/// ```\npub fn has_caret_prefix(field_name: &str) -> bool {\n    field_name.starts_with('^')\n}\n\n/// Extract a nested field from JSON using dot notation\npub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n    if path.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let mut current = value;\n    for part in path.split('.') {\n        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n            let key = &part[..bracket_pos];\n            let index_str = &part[bracket_pos + 1..part.len() - 1];\n            let index: usize = index_str.parse().ok()?;\n\n            current = current.get(key)?.get(index)?;\n        } else {\n            current = current.get(part)?;\n        }\n    }\n    Some(current.clone())\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from JSON\npub fn extract_string(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let field = extract_field(value, path)?;\n    match field {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse timestamp from various formats\npub fn parse_timestamp(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string(value, path)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Extract a field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// **Envelope-first with payload fallback for caret-prefixed paths:**\n/// - If path starts with `^`, try envelope first (remove `^` prefix)\n/// - If envelope is None OR field not found in envelope, fallback to payload\n/// - Otherwise, extract from payload only\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `^field`:**\n/// 1. Try `envelope.field` (if envelope exists)\n/// 2. Fallback to `payload.field` (if envelope missing or field not found)\n/// 3. Return None (if both fail)\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `field` (no caret):**\n/// - Extract from `payload.field` only\n///\n/// Supports dot notation for nested fields (e.g., `^outer.ts` or `user.role`)\n/// and array indexing (e.g., `items[0].name`).\npub fn extract_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<Value> {\n    if has_caret_prefix(path) {\n        // Strip the caret prefix\n        if let Some(envelope_path) = path.strip_prefix('^') {\n            // Try envelope first\n            if let Some(env) = envelope {\n                if let Some(value) = extract_field(env, envelope_path) {\n                    return Some(value); // Found in envelope\n                }\n            }\n            // Fallback to payload (using path without ^)\n            extract_field(payload, envelope_path)\n        } else {\n            // Should not happen due to starts_with check, but handle defensively\n            None\n        }\n    } else {\n        // No caret prefix - extract from payload only\n        extract_field(payload, path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_with_envelope` that converts the raw `Value` to a string,\n/// following the same coercion rules as `extract_string` (String, Number, Bool, Null).\npub fn extract_string_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    let value = extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)?;\n    match value {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        Value::Array(arr) => {\n            // Handle content arrays (e.g., Claude Code format with text blocks and tool calls)\n            // Extract text from all text blocks in the array\n            let text_parts: Vec<String> = arr\n                .iter()\n                .filter_map(|item| {\n                    if let Some(obj) = item.as_object() {\n                        // Check for text blocks: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"}\n                        if obj.get(\"type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some(\"text\") {\n                            return obj\n                                .get(\"text\")\n                                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    None\n                })\n                .collect();\n            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n            }\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n/// UTC-naive formats.\npub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Base trait for all format parsers\npub trait FormatParser {\n    /// Parse events from the source\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n\n    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n}\n\n/// metadata: Option<Value>,\n    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n    /// is a child of another session)\n    pub parent_session_id:      // Unicode and special characters\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^_field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^$field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^field-name\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^field_name\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^fieldName\"));\n\n        // Not a caret prefix\n        assert!(!has_caret_prefix(\" ^field\")); // space before
